Date: 2025-04-07

Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Asha Patel, Marco Diaz - Redwood; Erin Park, Samir Rao, Lilly Chen, Dave Ng - Stratos Labs
---
Summary:
Quick demo of key hierarchy (org vs project keys), rate/quotas patterns for multi-tenant apps, and console config walkthrough for fairshare routing and burst policies. Covered security controls (KMS, SSO) and next steps for a short pilot + data request.
Topics: tenant-level quotas, project keys, routing policies, burst windows, fairshare, billing segmentation, KMS and audit logs, pilot scope and benchmarking
Action items (briefed in call): see metadata list
---
00:00 Speaker 1 (Asha): okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Asha from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Marco, our solutions engineer. quick round of intros?
00:22 Speaker 2 (Erin): erin here — engineering manager, thanks for setting this up. we wanted to see how you do org-level controls, we've got a mix of internal and external tenants.
00:35 Speaker 1 (Asha): great, and Samir?
00:38 Speaker 3 (Samir): samir, cto. main questions: how do we isolate noisy customers, and how easy is it to map billing to our internal org structure.
00:50 Speaker 4 (Marco): yeah and i'll jump in with a demo — i'll show the console and a couple of examples, but quick note: our runtime supports org/project key hierarchy with sticky routing and fairshare, you can do per-project burst windows and global org-level quotas.
01:10 Speaker 2 (Erin): when you say "project key" is that a key we hand out to our customers or internal services?
01:16 Speaker 4 (Marco): good question — it's flexible. you can mint project keys per customer or per internal service. org key is the umbrella — think of it as the billing/owner scope. project keys inherit default quota rules from the org but can have overrides.
01:35 Speaker 3 (Samir): and what about tenant isolation on Dedicated vs Hosted? we prefer dedicated for some high-volume tenants.
01:42 Speaker 4 (Marco): Dedicated gives you capacity isolation — you can pin certain projects to dedicated pools. Hosted still supports project-level quotas but routes to shared capacity with fairshare so noisy tenants get throttled according to policy.
02:05 Speaker 1 (Asha): quick agenda: Marco will do a console walkthrough, then i'll go through cost/billing segmentation, then security.
02:18 Speaker 4 (Marco): starting the console — here is an org page, you'll see the org quota on top, we set token-per-minute and concurrency thresholds, there's a burst bucket. (pauses) sorry, screen's a bit slow — mm
02:40 Speaker 4 (Marco): so example: Stratos Org quota 1,000 rps, project keys for "partner-api" and "internal-worker" created. you can set project key quotas as absolute or as percentage of org. e.g., partner-api gets 30% guaranteed, remainder is pooled.
03:05 Speaker 2 (Erin): that percentage model is interesting — does that enforce at the router or at the scheduler level?
03:12 Speaker 4 (Marco): router level for immediate throttling decisions; scheduler/runtime applies backlog shaping. that's how we keep latency SLOs while enforcing fairshare.
03:30 Speaker 3 (Samir): and what happens during a sudden spike — do you have burst policies per project?
03:36 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, burst windows are per-project. you can define a short-term burst (e.g., 10s window with higher burst capacity) and a longer cooldown. also we have sticky routing for sessions so KV cache locality is preserved.
03:55 Speaker 5 (Lilly): how does that interact with KV cache? our embeddings-heavy flows are sensitive to cold cache.
04:02 Speaker 4 (Marco): sticky routing pins requests from the same project to the same serving lane when possible to keep KV cache warm. if pinned lane is overloaded, fallback kicks in to compatible model variant — small perf hit.
04:25 Speaker 2 (Erin): can we carve out a set of GPUs for very large tenants?
04:29 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, that's a Dedicated pool case — reserve a pool and map project keys to it. or on Hosted you request reserved capacity for specific projects via our Dedicated offering.
04:45 Speaker 1 (Asha): moving to quotas and billing — you can tag project keys with billing codes, we export token-level usage per key so you can map costs to teams or customers.
05:00 Speaker 3 (Samir): token-level data retention — how long do you keep it? this is important for auditing.
05:06 Speaker 5 (Lilly): yeah also need to know where logs live and KMS integration.
05:12 Speaker 1 (Asha): good call. we have configurable retention; default 90 days, longer retention as an add-on. logs and audit trails are in the private control plane for Private customers, and we integrate with customer KMS for key material.
05:28 Speaker 5 (Lilly): do you support customer-managed HSM?
05:31 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, HSM/KMS via standard providers — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer-hosted HSM for Private installs.
05:45 Speaker 2 (Erin): what about SSO and RBAC? we have multiple identity providers.
05:49 Speaker 1 (Asha): SSO (SAML/OIDC) plus SCIM for user provisioning and role-based access — you can scope roles to org, project, or route.
06:00 Speaker 3 (Samir): security is big for us. can you share SOC2 plus network diagrams?
06:05 Speaker 1 (Asha): absolutely, i'll attach SOC2, ISOs, and a network diagram.
06:12 Speaker 5 (Lilly): timing for that?
06:14 Speaker 1 (Asha): i'll send by Thursday 2025-04-10.
06:20 Speaker 4 (Marco): demo continued — here's policy config: you can create policies named "enterprise-default", "partner-strict", etc. Each policy can express rate limits per route, concurrency caps, and fairshare weights.
06:45 Speaker 2 (Erin): can a policy be applied to tags or labels? our services are named inconsistently.
06:51 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, policies can target project keys, tags, or route patterns. we also have grouping rules to map incoming keys to projects via header mapping.
07:05 Speaker 3 (Samir): what about auto-escalation — if an org exceeds billing thresholds, can you auto-suspend keys or throttle?
07:12 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, you can set billing thresholds with automatic throttles or suspend. we also support email/webhook alerts to your ops channel.
07:30 Speaker 2 (Erin): curious about the fairness algorithm — is it leaky-bucket, token-bucket, or something custom?
07:36 Speaker 4 (Marco): it's token-bucket at the edge, but we run a control loop that adapts pool weights based on usage, which gives better utilization and predictable SLOs.
07:55 Speaker 1 (Asha): quick interjection — competitor question: you mentioned OpenAI before, how are we positioned?
08:00 Speaker 4 (Marco): our differentiation is serving controls and observability for tenants — OpenAI doesn't give you the same kind of org/project quota primitives or on-prem options. InferX sometimes touts throughput but not the same operational surface.
08:20 Speaker 5 (Lilly): ok let's talk pilot — what does a pilot look like?
08:24 Speaker 1 (Asha): typically 4 weeks: week 0 onboarding and keying; week 1 routing and policy configuration; week 2 run shadow traffic and small canary; week 3 run measured benchmarks and tune. we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet and a short checklist.
08:42 Speaker 3 (Samir): ROI — can you estimate cost delta if we move ten of our partners to Dedicated?
08:48 Speaker 4 (Marco): rough estimate: Dedicated has fixed monthly pool cost + per-token usage. for 10 high-volume partners we estimate roughly 20-35% unit cost reduction depending on utilization; i'll follow up with a more concrete calc if you share traffic.
09:10 Speaker 2 (Erin): we've got two regulatory customers in EU — data residency matters. how do you support region pinning?
09:18 Speaker 4 (Marco): you can pin projects to regions and choose Private deployment in a customer VPC for strict residency. Hosted regions across EU also available.
09:30 Speaker 5 (Lilly): audit logs format — is it JSON-LD or other? we ingest into our SIEM.
09:35 Speaker 4 (Marco): JSON structured logs with event IDs; we can ship to your SIEM or S3.
09:45 Speaker 2 (Erin): any limits on number of project keys? we might have thousands.
09:48 Speaker 4 (Marco): we support large cardinality keys; for very large numbers we recommend grouping via logical projects to keep the console tidy.
10:05 Speaker 1 (Asha): okay Marco, show an example of policy that throttles by route.
10:10 Speaker 4 (Marco): sure, here's a route pattern /v1/generate/partner* with a policy limiting to 500 rpm per project, with a 20% guaranteed share — if a project exceeds its guaranteed share, it can still use pooled capacity until the org cap is hit. (pauses) some log lines here are slightly delayed — transcription note.
10:35 Speaker 2 (Erin): how does billing segmentation work at token-level — do you provide daily exports?
10:40 Speaker 1 (Asha): yes, daily exports, and we have a streaming usage endpoint for near-real-time consumption.
10:55 Speaker 3 (Samir): about enforcement: if a project hits its concurrency cap, do calls fail fast or queue?
11:00 Speaker 4 (Marco): config option — fail fast for latency-sensitive routes, or queue with low-priority preemption for batch jobs.
11:18 Speaker 5 (Lilly): for our embeddings pipelines we'd prefer queueing with backpressure rather than failures.
11:22 Speaker 4 (Marco): totally supported. you can also set separate classes for embeddings vs generation.
11:35 Speaker 2 (Erin): one more on quotas: can we express both token and request quotas?
11:39 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, token-based and request-based quotas are orthogonal and can be combined in a policy.
11:50 Speaker 1 (Asha): quick demo pivot — in Optimize we run suggestions for batching and quantization; if we detect many short prompt patterns we suggest batching to reduce unit cost.
12:05 Speaker 3 (Samir): will Optimize recommend model variants? we run some gen workloads and some reranking.
12:12 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes, Optimize will recommend compatible lower-cost quantized variants, and show expected token-cost savings and latency impact.
12:30 Speaker 2 (Erin): any gotchas when combined with quotas? like switching model variants affects KV cache locality?
12:36 Speaker 4 (Marco): can affect cache locality — Optimize flags those and suggests sticky routing policies to preserve performance during model switchovers.
12:55 Speaker 5 (Lilly): do you have sample IaC to provision policies?
12:59 Speaker 4 (Marco): yes we have Terraform + API snippets; i'll share a repo link in the follow-up.
13:10 Speaker 1 (Asha): okay wrapping up, quick recap and next steps — we'll send SOC2 docs and network diagram, Marco will send a perf snapshot and Terraform snippets, and we agreed on pilot scope.
13:28 Speaker 2 (Erin): timeline: procurement by end of May, pilot kickoff week of 2025-04-21.
13:35 Speaker 1 (Asha): perfect — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff and attach the checklist and benchmark sheet.
13:46 Speaker 3 (Samir): thanks all.
